Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a large right-sided pneumothorax with complete collapse of the right lung and marked mediastinal shift to the right, causing the cardiac silhouette to appear displaced into the right hemithorax. This appearance is characteristic of right-sided cardiac herniation through a pericardial defect (often post-pneumonectomy), which leads to acute haemodynamic compromise via torsion and obstruction of the great vessels.
